## Key Concepts

1. its a spectrum 
  rigid <--------------------------------------------------------------------------------> flexible 
  linear    lasso/ridge   logistic regression   trees   random forest   boosting    neural networks 
  
  parametric: assume a functional form, only need to know y intercept and slope
  non-parametric: wiggly, lots of things to estimate
  
2. the line
  gap between observed and predicted is the residual/error 
  least squares - minimize sum for squared errors
  noise in Y goes into the residuals (not noise)
  noise in x tends to flatten the slope 
  
3. fit vs. prediction
  R^2 - on the data it was fit to 
  test/train - 80% of data for training, 20% of data for test
  RMSE -> lower is better!
  
4. cross validation (new CV)
  k-fold -> 5 fold for 100 records
  break data up into groups of 20, take turn training vs testing each group 
  overfitting - learn the noise
  
5. how to pick features 
  multicollinearity -> mostly harmless for this application, but check 
  plotted residuals chould look random -> homoskedastic 
  heteroskedastic: shows a pattern -> indication that something is missing from the model
